protocols.name: Ordinals inscriptions (tapscript envelope)
protocols.description: Arbitrary content (text, JSON, images) embedded in a taproot script-path spend via the 'ord' envelope: OP_FALSE OP_IF PUSH('ord') ...tag/value pairs... OP_0 ...body chunks... OP_ENDIF inside the tapscript witness element. Reveal tx carries the data; content-type and body are recoverable client-side.
protocols.detection: For each vin: vin[].witness is an array of hex strings. A tx is an inscription reveal if any witness element w contains the substring "0063036f7264" at an EVEN character index (00=OP_FALSE, 63=OP_IF, 03=push-3, 6f7264='ord'). In verified samples it sits in vin[0].witness[1] (the tapscript, second-to-last element; last is the control block), typically preceded by "20<32-byte-pubkey>ac" (PUSH32 pk OP_CHECKSIG). Alternative field: vin[].inner_witnessscript_asm contains "OP_0 OP_IF OP_PUSHBYTES_3 6f7264" (VERIFIED present for P2TR script-path spends). Content-type extraction: after the envelope marker, parse script pushes; a push of single byte 0x01 (hex "0101") is the content-type tag and the NEXT push is the MIME string, e.g. "18746578742f706c61696e3b636861727365743d7574662d38" = PUSH24 'text/plain;charset=utf-8'. Body: everything after the empty push OP_0 (hex "00"), concatenating each data push (max 520 bytes each, prefixed 0x4c/0x4d for PUSHDATA1/2) until OP_ENDIF (0x68). Payload size = sum of body push lengths.
protocols.prevalence: 370 of 29,562 txs (~1.3%) across 7 blocks at heights 957508-957515; ~96% of them are BRC-20 transfers. Non-BRC20 example is a .bitmap text inscription.

protocols.name: BRC-20
protocols.description: Fungible-token metaprotocol riding on Ordinals: the inscription body is JSON with "p":"brc-20" (ops: deploy/mint/transfer). Verified sample bodies: {"p":"brc-20","op":"transfer","amt":"700000000000","tick":"sats"} and {"p":"brc-20","op":"transfer","tick":"$-:)","amt":"13700"}.
protocols.detection: First match the Ordinals envelope ("0063036f7264" in a vin[].witness element, even index). Then reassemble the envelope body (concat data pushes after the OP_0 separator) and JSON.parse it; classify BRC-20 if parsed.p === "brc-20". Content-type in verified samples is 'text/plain;charset=utf-8'. Fast pre-filter: witness element hex contains "6272632d3230" (ASCII 'brc-20') at even index — works in practice because the string sits near the start of the first 520-byte chunk, but parse-then-JSON.parse is the robust check (whitespace variants like {"p": "brc-20"} exist and key order is not fixed).
protocols.prevalence: 356 of 29,562 txs across 7 recent blocks (~1.2%) — nearly all current ordinals activity is BRC-20 transfers.

protocols.name: Runes / Runestones
protocols.description: Casey Rodarmor's fungible-token protocol. Protocol message ('runestone') is an OP_RETURN output whose first pushed opcode is OP_13, followed by LEB128-varint payload (edicts/etchings/mints). By far the dominant data protocol in mid-2026.
protocols.detection: Any vout with vout[].scriptpubkey_type === "op_return" AND vout[].scriptpubkey hex STARTING with "6a5d" (6a=OP_RETURN, 5d=OP_13/OP_PUSHNUM_13). vout[].scriptpubkey_asm starts "OP_RETURN OP_PUSHNUM_13" followed by OP_PUSHBYTES_N or OP_PUSHDATA1 and the varint payload. Verified examples: script "6a5d0a1600ff7f8188ec8ad02b" (13-byte script), "6a5d321600..." (53 bytes), and a 196-byte runestone "6a5d4cc01600..." (note OP_PUSHDATA1 4c for >75-byte payloads). The runestone is usually NOT vout[0] — verified samples have it at vout[2]/vout[3]. Must anchor the match at position 0 of the hex string.
protocols.prevalence: Massive: 16,491 of 29,562 txs (~56%) across 7 blocks (957508-957515); per-block share ranged 17% to 92% (block 957508: 6,175 of 6,692 txs). 138 of 163 >80-byte OP_RETURNs in those blocks were large runestones.

protocols.name: Bitcoin Stamps / SRC-20 (bare multisig data embedding)
protocols.description: Data hidden in fake pubkeys of bare 1-of-3 multisig outputs (unprunable UTXO bloat). Modern SRC-20 (post-block-796000, off Counterparty) ARC4-encrypts '2-byte BE length + "stamp:" + JSON' keyed by the first input's txid. Verified decode: stamp:{"p":"src-20","op":"transfer","tick":"MSKK","amt":"100000"}.
protocols.detection: vout[].scriptpubkey_type === "multisig" (authoritative; scriptpubkey = 51 [21 <33B pk>]x3 53 ae, asm ends "OP_PUSHNUM_3 OP_CHECKMULTISIG", 105-byte script). Decode to confirm SRC-20: for each multisig vout in order, extract the 33-byte pubkeys; drop the LAST pubkey (real signer key); from each remaining pubkey strip the first byte (02/03 sign) and last byte (nonce) leaving 31 bytes; concatenate across all multisig vouts; RC4/ARC4-decrypt with key = hex-decoded vin[0].txid (displayed big-endian order, NOT reversed — empirically verified); result = uint16BE length + payload starting "stamp:" (hex 7374616d703a) + JSON with "p":"src-20". Classic Stamps (base64 images) ride Counterparty issuances in the same multisig encoding but decrypt to lengthByte+"CNTRPRTY" instead.
protocols.prevalence: A few txs per block currently (e.g. block 957513 had multiple SRC-20 transfers). Note: OLGA-era stamps use fake P2WSH outputs instead, which are NOT byte-detectable from scriptpubkey (see gotchas).

protocols.name: Counterparty (CNTRPRTY, ARC4-encoded)
protocols.description: Oldest asset metaprotocol; still alive at low volume (sends, MPMA multi-sends, dispensers). Data is ARC4(RC4)-obfuscated with the first input's previous-txid as key, in either an OP_RETURN output (short messages) or bare multisig outputs (longer messages like MPMA).
protocols.detection: OP_RETURN form: vout[].scriptpubkey_type === "op_return"; parse the pushdata after 0x6a (handle direct push <=75, 0x4c PUSHDATA1, 0x4d PUSHDATA2); ARC4-decrypt with key = bytes of hex string vin[0].txid EXACTLY as returned by the API (no byte reversal — verified: decrypt of tx bc75d6b8... vout[0] script "6a2b9893040b6c36..." yields b'CNTRPRTY\x02...' = enhanced_send). Match decrypted[0:8] === "CNTRPRTY" (hex 434e545250525459); byte 8+ is the message-type id. Multisig form: identical pubkey-data extraction as SRC-20 above (drop last pubkey, strip first/last byte of each, concat, ARC4 with vin[0].txid); decrypted stream = 1 chunk-length byte + "CNTRPRTY" + message (verified on 2 MPMA txs: b'=CNTRPRTY\x03...'). So a client-side CNTRPRTY check needs ONE ARC4 implementation applied to both output shapes; ARC4 is ~15 lines of JS.
protocols.prevalence: Rare: 1 OP_RETURN Counterparty tx found in 10 fully-scanned blocks; Counterparty API shows ~1 tx per 2-10 blocks (mix of op_return and multisig encodings).

protocols.name: Large OP_RETURN (>80-byte datacarrier, post-Core-30)
protocols.description: Bitcoin Core v30 (Oct 2025) raised default datacarrier policy to ~100kB and allowed multiple OP_RETURN outputs, so >80-byte OP_RETURNs now relay standardly. Per Optech #393, large OP_RETURNs were ~0.44% of OP_RETURN data bytes over blocks 915800-936000; in blocks 957508-957515 I measured 163 outputs with script >83 bytes (~23/block) — 85% large runestones, most of the rest 'ACME'.
protocols.detection: vout[].scriptpubkey_type === "op_return" AND (scriptpubkey.length / 2) > 83. Rationale: an 80-byte payload script is 1(6a)+1(4c)+1(len)+80 = 83 bytes, so >83 total script bytes implies payload >80 bytes. To get exact payload size, parse push opcodes after 0x6a: direct push (<=0x4b), 0x4c PUSHDATA1 (1 length byte), 0x4d PUSHDATA2 (2 LE length bytes). Verified samples: 91-byte script "6a4c5841434d45..." (88B ACME payload), 85-byte "6a4c5241434d45...", 196-byte "6a5d4cc0..." (large runestone — classify runes first, use this as fallback bucket).
protocols.prevalence: ~20-140 outputs per block depending on runes activity; dedicated large-datacarrier (non-runes) users ~5-10/block currently.

protocols.name: ACME (2026 asset metaprotocol, dual encoding)
protocols.description: Currently-active but publicly undocumented asset/file metaprotocol (web searches find no spec; asset names like 'PEPECHART.ED' suggest Counterparty-community lineage). Two encodings, both verified live: (a) OP_RETURN messages = ASCII 'ACME' + 2 version/flag bytes + zlib stream (0x789c) containing TLV asset ops; (b) tapscript envelope OP_FALSE OP_IF PUSH('acme') carrying large files — verified sample held a 61KB image/png named 'QUEEN' with TLV body 01<content-type> 02<name> ... + zlib data.
protocols.detection: OP_RETURN form: vout[].scriptpubkey_type === "op_return" and the pushed payload begins hex "41434d45" ('ACME') — with PUSHDATA1 the script starts "6a4c__41434d45" (e.g. "6a4c5241434d45", "6a4c5841434d45"), so check payload-start not script-start; zlib magic 789c appears at payload offset 9. Envelope form: any vin[].witness element contains "00630461636d65" at even index (OP_FALSE OP_IF PUSH4 'acme'), or vin[].inner_witnessscript_asm contains "OP_0 OP_IF OP_PUSHBYTES_4 61636d65" (both verified). Unlike ord, the acme envelope can start at byte 0 of the witness element (no leading pubkey/OP_CHECKSIG) — do a substring search, not an anchored one.
protocols.prevalence: 43 ACME OP_RETURN outputs + 9 acme envelopes across 7 blocks (~6-7 txs/block) — currently the second-most-common OP_RETURN protocol after Runes and the main non-runes user of >80-byte OP_RETURNs.

protocols.name: Taproot annex usage
protocols.description: Annex-carrying inputs (a P2TR witness whose final element starts 0x50) were discussed as a future data vector, but annex-bearing txs are still non-standard for relay and effectively absent from blocks: ZERO found in ~29,500 txs across 7 fully-parsed recent blocks. Include the check for completeness; expect no hits.
protocols.detection: vin[].witness.length >= 2 AND vin[].witness[witness.length-1] starts with hex "50". Only meaningful when vin[].prevout.scriptpubkey_type === "v1_p2tr". If present, the annex is the last element and shifts the tapscript/control-block positions up by one — relevant to ord-envelope element indexing.
protocols.prevalence: 0 observed in ~29,500 recent txs (blocks 957508-957515). Not currently a real-world spam vector.

protocols.name: Atomicals (ARC-20, 'atom' envelope)
protocols.description: Ordinals-like protocol using tapscript envelope OP_FALSE OP_IF PUSH('atom'). Effectively dead in 2026 — zero occurrences in ~29,500 recent txs. Keep the pattern only if you want to classify historical (2023-2024) transactions.
protocols.detection: Any vin[].witness element contains "00630461746f6d" at even index (00=OP_FALSE, 63=OP_IF, 04=push-4, 61746f6d='atom'); or vin[].inner_witnessscript_asm contains "OP_0 OP_IF OP_PUSHBYTES_4 61746f6d". Same envelope mechanics as ord (payload pushes until OP_ENDIF).
protocols.prevalence: 0 observed in ~29,500 recent txs; historical protocol only.

gotchas: Hex-substring alignment: when grepping witness/scriptpubkey hex strings for byte patterns (6a5d, 0063036f7264, 6272632d3230), require indexOf(pattern) % 2 === 0, or you will match nibble-misaligned garbage.

Runes must be anchored: scriptpubkey.startsWith("6a5d") AND scriptpubkey_type === "op_return". The bytes 6a5d occurring mid-script, inside a pubkey, or inside witness data mean nothing — OP_RETURN is always the first opcode of a datacarrier output.

Bare-multisig false positive (hit this in practice): a naive raw-script heuristic 'starts 0x51-0x53 and ends 0xae' also matches P2TR outputs (5120 + 32-byte key whose last byte happens to be 0xae) — tx 4a18ac6519f0e1da413e8b9ce93914ce0340f619322092bd131e96b6cb4d6642 is such a P2TR-only tx. Always trust mempool.space's vout[].scriptpubkey_type === "multisig" instead of pattern-matching the script yourself.

Witness element ordering: for P2TR script-path the tapscript is witness[len-2] and the control block is witness[len-1]; if an annex is present (last element starts 0x50) everything shifts by one. Simplest robust classifier: scan EVERY element of every vin's witness for envelope patterns.

Envelope position within the tapscript varies: ord envelopes usually follow '20<pubkey>ac' (so 0063036f7264 appears ~35 bytes in), but acme envelopes were found starting at byte 0 of the witness element. Substring-search, don't anchor.

Inscription bodies are split into <=520-byte pushes with interleaved length prefixes (0x4c/0x4d + length). A hex grep for a JSON keyword can miss when the string straddles a push boundary. Correct approach: parse the envelope (tag/value push pairs until the empty push OP_0/0x00, then concat all body pushes until OP_ENDIF 0x68), THEN JSON.parse. This also handles BRC-20 whitespace/key-order variants — do not grep for the exact string '{"p":"brc-20"'.

Content-type extraction: envelope tag pushes are data pushes, so the content-type tag is hex '0101' (push of byte 0x01) followed by a push of the MIME string; tag 0x07 = parent, 0x05 = CBOR metadata, etc. Payload size = sum of body push lengths, NOT witness element length.

OP_RETURN payload parsing: payload can sit behind a direct push (<=0x4b), OP_PUSHDATA1 (0x4c, 1 length byte) or OP_PUSHDATA2 (0x4d, 2 LE length bytes) — offsets differ. For the >80-byte test, (scriptpubkey.length/2) > 83 is a safe threshold (83 = 1+1+1+80).

Protocol overlap and priority: one tx can match several patterns — a 196-byte runestone is both 'runes' and 'large OP_RETURN' (9d8ce1d0...); nearly all ordinals are also BRC-20. Classify specific protocols first (runes, ACME, CNTRPRTY, ord/brc-20), use 'large datacarrier' as the fallback bucket.

Coinbase false positives: EVERY coinbase has an OP_RETURN starting aa21a9ed (SegWit witness commitment — consensus-required, not spam), plus merge-mining/sidechain tags (RSKB = Rootstock, CORE, EXSA = ExSat). Skip txs where vin[0].is_coinbase === true.

Not all small OP_RETURNs are 'spam': prefix histogram of 7 blocks shows THORChain memos ('=:', 'OUT:', '=|', 'to:'), Stacks block-commits (prefix 'X2[' hex 58325b), exchange tags, etc. These are <=80-byte functional messages; decide whether your classifier flags them.

Counterparty ARC4 key direction (verified empirically): key = bytes.fromHex(vin[0].txid) using the txid EXACTLY as the API displays it (big-endian) — do NOT reverse. ARC4 == RC4; ~15 lines of JS. The OP_RETURN form decrypts to 'CNTRPRTY'+msg directly; the multisig form decrypts to 1 length byte + 'CNTRPRTY'; SRC-20 stamps decrypt to 2-byte BE length + 'stamp:'.

Multisig data extraction detail: use only the first N-1 of the 33-byte pubkeys per output (the last is the signer's real key), and strip the first byte (02/03 fake sign) AND the last byte (nonce) of each, giving 31 data bytes per fake key; concatenate across multisig outputs in vout order before decrypting.

OLGA-era Stamps (post-2024 option) embed data as fake P2WSH scripthashes — vout[].scriptpubkey_type is a perfectly normal 'v0_p2wsh', so they are NOT byte-detectable from the output script; only heuristics work (long runs of equal dust-value P2WSH outputs in one tx). Multisig SRC-20 is still actively used though (verified in blocks 957512-957513).

mempool.space API practicalities: /api/tx/:txid works for unconfirmed mempool txs too; vin[].witness is already split per element (hex strings, no length prefixes); vin[].inner_witnessscript_asm IS populated for P2TR script-path spends (not just P2WSH) and can be string-matched for 'OP_0 OP_IF OP_PUSHBYTES_3 6f7264'; block tx listing pages 25 at a time (/api/block/:hash/txs/:start_index) — for bulk scanning fetch /api/block/:hash/raw instead (one request, parse locally); unauthenticated API is rate-limited, so throttle rapid paging.

Prevalence snapshot (blocks 957508-957515, 2026-07-10, 29,562 txs): Runes ~56% of ALL txs (per-block 17%-92%), ordinals/BRC-20 ~1.3%, ACME ~6-7 txs/block, SRC-20 multisig a few/block, Counterparty ~1 per 5-10 blocks, >80B OP_RETURN ~23 outputs/block, taproot annex 0, Atomicals 0. A fee-market-aware classifier should optimize the runes path first.

Working scripts from this research (raw block parser/classifier, ARC4, envelope parser, verifier): /tmp/claude-1000/-home-cbspears/bd2433b4-fcf1-4214-87af-6b2dc71942b5/scratchpad/btc/rawscan.py and verify.py.
